explanation.definitionFit: An albert is the short heavy chain fixing a pocket watch to a waistcoat buttonhole, named for Queen Victoria's consort.

clue.text: Manual confused old student

blocks.note: taken as written

taken as written

clue.text: Organiser of type that's been superseded

definitions.text: Organiser of type that's been superseded

blocks.clueFragment: Organiser of type that's been superseded
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who arranges an outdated sort or category of thing
setter's reading: a printing worker who set metal letters by hand, a trade replaced by computer setting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' reads as kind or sort; here it is printing type, and it is the job, not the type, that has been replaced.

clue.text: Excellent river harbour in Shannon, for example

explanation.surface: A fine river haven on the Shannon in Ireland.

explanation.definitionFit: Shannon in County Clare is an international airport, so it is one instance of the answer.

clue.text: Audacity producing narrow margin of victory

explanation.surface: Boldness pays off in a close win.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass neck is British slang for impudence, and a horse winning by a neck wins by a tiny distance.

clue.text: Girl bound, so to speak, to be suspicious

indicators.note: so to speak means as it would be said out loud, signalling sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: Miss is a title for a girl

explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust is to doubt or lack confidence in someone, so to be suspicious of them.

clue.text: Biscuit of the type flower-girl picked up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' sounds like bought or collected, but in a down clue it lifts the word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a thin rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream.

clue.text: Some ideas I erroneously viewed as relatively simple

explanation.surface: Someone reckons a few of the notions were mistakenly thought to be less difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Easier is the comparative of easy, so it means simpler than something else, matching relatively simple.

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Food obtained from palm a short time previously

explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch taken from the pith of the sago palm and used in puddings.

clue.text: Ways in which a tiger is different, in general

blocks.note: two lots of ST, the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written

clue.text: Author first captures East African animals

explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest, or gnu, are large antelopes of the African plains; the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Novices in convent finally accepted by religious leaders

explanation.walkthrough: In British sports slang a rabbit is a poor or inexperienced player, especially a weak batsman in cricket.

clue.text: This type of herring is included in British fish

explanation.definitionFit: Brisling is the sprat, a small fish of the herring family canned as sardines in Norway.

clue.text: Total score halved in squash

explanation.definitionFit: To squash something is to crush it flat, which is what flatten means as a verb.

clue.text: Old way to convert weapon

clue.text: Equipment for lifting fish on line

clue.text: Shape material, do, to produce this

blocks.note: taken as written
